summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Card fees have staying power
articles.description: Merchants keep attacking the fees, but the charges keep coming because consumers love swiping their cards.

articles.title: Is the nickel nearing a revamp?
articles.description: It costs 13 cents to produce the five-cent coin. Congress wants the U.S. to explore more cost-effective methods.

articles.title: RTP gears up for int’l reach
articles.description: The Bank of New York and other financial institutions are preparing for a pilot next year that will stretch the real-time payments network across borders.

articles.title: Priority Tech buys IntelliPay for up to $15M
articles.description: The payments company is gaining a new government payments business with its deal for Utah-based IntelliPay.

articles.title: Building Block’s Square base
articles.description: The fintech is expanding its efforts to market local restaurants using its point-of-sale system across Cash App’s user base.

articles.title: Amex’s low fraud rate turns on its closed system
articles.description: More access to cardholder and merchant data also gives the card network an edge in fraud detection over its rivals.

articles.title: Walmart adds digital wallet options
articles.description: The mega-retailer said it will now accept Apple Pay and Google Pay payments, using tap-to-pay with smartwatches, contactless cards and phones.

articles.title: Stripe tips toward staying private
articles.description: The payments giant’s founders told investors that the company’s private structure will help it to be more nimble amid AI shifts.
